basis: Diaphragmatic, limb and skull defects with severe pulmonary hypoplasia define the syndrome; omphalocele occurred in only 1/4 reported fetuses.
Complex I deficiency with lactic acidosis; developmental impairment and hypertrophic cardiomyopathy each reported in 1/1 patient; respiratory insufficiency lacks a defined pulmonary lesion.
Trypanosoma cruzi infection directly damages myocardium and the cardiac conduction system.
Developmental communication disorder affecting speech production; structural airway disease does not characterize the umbrella.
Benign neoplasm of the scrotum, classified here as a male reproductive organ; no specific cutaneous or vascular origin is established.
Neurodevelopmental disorder; strabismus in 4/4 and hyperopic astigmatism in 30-79% support ocular dysfunction; sparse hair and long fingers do not establish additional organ damage.
Inherited megakaryocyte proliferation and sustained thrombocytosis; thrombotic complications are not established as affecting at least 30%.
Atherosclerotic thrombotic occlusion of the distal abdominal aorta; claudication alone does not establish skeletal muscle damage.
Syndrome defined by ichthyosis with abnormal epidermal keratohyalin granules and intellectual disability.
Non-hereditary malignant retinal tumor; the tumor's origin is ocular.
Umbrella includes the common asymptomatic peripheral form; liver injury, cataracts and developmental impairment characterize the rare generalized form and its phenotype annotations.
Inherited disruption of proline metabolism; neurologic and connective-tissue manifestations vary across subtypes and are not universal across this umbrella.
Disease of oral mucosa, which belongs to the gastrointestinal axis.
Intramural outpouchings of gallbladder mucosa; the gallbladder belongs to the hepatic axis.
Congenital rudimentary supernumerary postaxial digit; a limb malformation.
Paralysis of all four limbs represents neurologic motor loss; secondary muscle wasting does not define this concept.
Juvenile-onset inflammatory keratinization disorder of the skin; an autoimmune or infectious mechanism is not established for the umbrella.
Cataracts 80-99%; intrinsic insulin resistance and hearing loss 30-79%; GI dysfunction omitted by cap; cardiac involvement <30%. Diabetes alone is not the endocrine basis.
Sterol biosynthesis disorder with defining neurodevelopmental defects; cataracts and aortic stenosis each 30-79%; syndactyly omitted by cap; renal ectopia has only a single-case report.
Inherited sulfur-metabolism defect causes circulating malodorous compounds; extraoral halitosis does not establish oral or pulmonary damage.
Biofilm-associated inflammatory destruction of tooth-supporting periodontal tissues; these tissues belong to the oral gastrointestinal axis.
Neoplasm of the lymphoid system; the umbrella includes benign non-lymphoma tumors, so a lymphoma-specific immune label is not universal.
IgG4-mediated retroperitoneal fibrosis; ureteral obstruction/renal impairment and large-vessel vasculitis occur in 30-79%; secondary anemia does not establish direct blood damage.
Developmental disability and dental/palatal defects define the syndrome; clubfoot and hypermetropia each occur in 30-79%; sparse hair alone is cosmetic.
Skeletal dysplasia and auditory canal atresia with hearing loss in 4/4; feeding difficulty/high palate do not establish GI damage; respiratory distress occurred in 1/4.
